canonical_statement: The study introduces RadFusion to make radiology report generation threshold-controllable so diagnostic text can be aligned with classifier operating points along the sensitivity-specificity trade-off.

RadFusion fuses three components: a calibrated multi-label image classifier, a VQA-based radiology report generator, and an LLM rewriter that makes stated diagnoses conform to thresholded classifier decisions while preserving report detail.
The perception component produces confidence scores for 14 CheXpert disease classes and binarizes each class at a selected threshold into positive or negative decisions.

The default perception model fine-tunes MedImageInsight for the CheXpert classes using an image-text plus image-class hybrid contrastive objective; the underlying MedImageInsight model has a 360M-parameter image encoder and 252M-parameter language encoder and was pretrained on more than 3.5 million medical image-text pairs across 12 imaging domains.
Classifier confidence scores are calibrated by post-hoc temperature scaling that learns a scalar temperature on a validation set to minimize Expected Calibration Error without changing AUC.

QRad reframes report generation as Auto-VQA: a question generator proposes clinically relevant questions from the image and an answer generator produces one report sentence per question, with the final report formed by concatenating the answers.

When thresholding changes an omitted disease class to positive, RadFusion queries QRad for a grounded follow-up description of that finding; the initial report plus follow-up answers form the evidence pool for rewriting.

The LLM rewriter keeps already-consistent positive findings, adds or corrects positive findings using the evidence pool when needed, removes or negates findings assigned negative, and preserves non-class content.

The proposed three-dimensional extension uses per-class thresholds Ta and Tb to define negative, semi-positive, and positive confidence zones and a third threshold Tc for urgency; this extension is presented as achievable by changing rewriting instructions without retraining the models.

Experiments use MIMIC-CXR, described as containing 227,835 studies and 377,110 chest X-ray images; the Findings section is the generation target and all evaluations use the official test split of 2,347 studies.

Threshold controllability is evaluated in a closed loop: classifier scores are thresholded, the LLM rewrites the QRad report to match those decisions, GPT-5 maps the rewritten report back to class labels, and the extracted labels are compared with ground-truth labels to calculate sensitivity and false-positive rate.

The evaluation sweeps a common threshold from 0.0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.1, yielding 11 operating points across 13 disease classes; No Finding is excluded because it overlaps semantically with the absence of other classes.
Threshold-controlled report performance is summarized by ROC curves plotting sensitivity against false-positive rate across operating points and by AUC-ROC across those points.

outcome.definition: ROC curve over threshold operating points; AUC summarizes discriminative performance.

canonical_statement: Under the prompt tuned for GPT-5, GPT-5.4 does not outperform GPT-5, which the authors interpret as evidence that rewriting prompts may need model-specific optimization.

The sample clinical interface presents per-class threshold sliders with predicted confidence, highlights the corresponding ROC operating point, displays the adjusted report, and links rewritten text spans to their disease class, confidence, and threshold.

The full LLM rewriting instruction contains a task description, a per-class template dictionary with positive and negative text examples, worked rewriting rules, and an output constraint requiring a JSON object containing only the modified report.
For the full 13-class threshold-control evaluation, the disease labels used as ground truth are obtained from the reference reports with VisualCheXbert.

The authors conclude that RadFusion makes generated radiology reports clinically adaptable, quantitatively evaluable, and diagnostically more accurate by conforming report content to threshold-adjusted classifier predictions.
Classifier errors can propagate into the rewritten report because RadFusion depends on the quality of the perception component.
The report generator may omit findings, limiting the evidence available to the rewriting stage.
The LLM rewriter may introduce subtle linguistic artifacts.

The rewriting instruction is template-based and tuned for chest X-ray findings, varies in effectiveness across LLMs, and would require retuning for a different rewriter, imaging modality, or clinical domain.
Threshold control operates over a predefined set of disease classes, so findings outside that set are not subject to threshold adjustment.
The evaluation relies on automatic label extraction from reports, which may itself introduce error.
The authors state that RadFusion is intended to assist rather than replace radiologist review.
